To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two novel mutations and a large deletion in PLA2-G6 gene are associated with an atypical and severe form of neuroaxonal dystrophies.
two novel mutations in the PLA2G6 were found in two patients with a rapidly progressive form of INAD.

we identified two novel splice-site PLA2G6 mutations in two INAD patients with an unusually rapid progression of the disorder and a novel genomic rearrangement in the same gene in another INAD patient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a novel PLA2G6 rearrangement, the first one reported in INAD patients and with the description of two novel splice-site alterations.
the molecular analysis of PLA2G6 in a cohort of INAD patients, and the identification of novel mutations, including a genomic rearrangement.
the identification of novel mutations in patients with PLA2G6-related neurodegenerative diseases and the molecular characterization of the genomic rearrangement underlying one of them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PLA2G6 mutations are responsible for both INAD and NBIA and that the clinical presentation is related to the residual protein activity, with a complete absence of iPLA2 activity leading to a more severe phenotype.
PLA2G6 mutations can cause either NBIA or INAD, but not both, with a few exceptions.
the absence of iPLA2 activity leads to the more severe form of INAD while residual iPLA2 activities are associated to a milder form of INAD or NBIA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1. the two novel mutations are likely responsible for the disease in the two patients, 2.
we have found a new genetic cause of INAD.
the PLA2G6-related disorders are characterized by a wide spectrum of clinical features, ranging from a mild NBIA to an early onset, rapidly progressive and severe INAD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a rapid disease progression and neuroradiological findings of brain iron accumulation are not sufficient to distinguish between INAD and NBIA.
the clinical phenotype of patients carrying a complete loss-of-function of PLA2G6 can be extremely variable, ranging from a severe INAD to a mild NBIA.

, despite the rarity of this disease, the identification of the causative mutation in a patient affected by infantile neuroaxional dystrophy is crucial to provide a genetic diagnosis and to offer genetic counselling to the parents.
